title: Georgy Fedorovich Horoshkoff-Morehodoff

17 MAR. 1943
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
No. 232
Date. 22-3-43
Foreign Affairs
Crime & Special Branch
Station........................................ File No.................... Date 16 March, 1943.
SUBJECT. G.F. Horoshkoff- Morehodoff.
With reference to the instruction of the Officer i/c
Foreign Affairs Crime & Special Branch enquiries made re
G.F.Horoshkoff show the following:-
Georgy Fedorovich Horoshkoff- Morehodoff Russian
emigrant, ortodox born on April 10, 1898 at Moscow. He is
in possession of French Residential Certificate No 3990
issued by the French Police on 15.10.42 on the strenght
of Card d'Identite (Identity Card) No 9712 issued by
the French Police in which he was mentioned as Russian
emigrant.Nothing is known regarding document Horoshkoff
produced when he first registered at the French Police.
Recently Horoshkoff made an application to the Russian
Emigrants Committee regarding registration as a Russian
emigrant and applied for an Emigrants passport. In his
application he stated that he did not know before announcement of Chairman of R.E.C. that it is necessary to all
Russian emigrants to have such passports.
Horoshkoff according to statment in his application
to Russian Emigrants Committee was educated at Commercial
School of M.U.Lermantoff in Moscow and subsequently in
Realnoe Uohilische/Middle School/ and for two months at
Building Construction faculty of Polytechnicum.He studied
until October 1916 when he joined Russian Army as a conscript serving at 19th Battery of Horse Artillery attache
to IIth Cavallery Division. After participating in the
First Great War he for a period according information
received served in the Red Army. In 1924 Horoshkoff arrived from Vladivostok to Harbin vis Pogranichnaia Station
In Harbin he was employed as a book keeper with the firms
Kabalkin,Yacobsen andothers and also was engaged in commerce ,owned a book store.

主题：G.F. Horoshkoff- Morehodoff。
遵照外事罪案与特别股主管官员的指示，就 G.F. Horoshkoff 进行的调查情况如下：
Georgy Fedorovich Horoshkoff- Morehodoff，俄罗斯流亡者，东正教徒，1898年4月10日出生于莫斯科。他持有法国警察局于1942年10月15日签发的第3990号法国居住证，该证系依据法国警察局签发的第9712号身份证（Card d'Identite）办理，证上注明其为俄罗斯流亡者。关于 Horoshkoff 首次在法国警察局登记时出示的文件，目前一无所知。
最近，Horoshkoff 向俄罗斯流亡者委员会申请登记为俄罗斯流亡者，并申请了流亡者护照。他在申请书中称，在俄罗斯流亡者委员会主席发布公告之前，他并不知道所有俄罗斯流亡者都必须持有此类护照。
根据 Horoshkoff 向俄罗斯流亡者委员会提交的申请书中的陈述，他曾在莫斯科 M.U. Lermantoff 商业学校受教育，随后在 Realnoe Uohilische（实科中学/中学）就读，并在理工学院建筑系学习了两个月。他一直学习到1916年10月，随后作为应征入伍者加入俄国军队，在隶属于第十一骑兵师的第十九炮兵连服役。参加第一次世界大战后，据收到的消息，他曾一度在红军中服役。1924年，Horoshkoff 经 Pogranichnaia 车站从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达哈尔滨。在哈尔滨，他受雇于 Kabalkin、Yacobsen 等公司担任簿记员，同时也从事商业活动，拥有一家书店。

Station........................................ File No.................... Date....................................

SUBJECT:
Until 1937 Horoshkoff was in possession of expired USSR
passport , according to his statement. In 1937 Horoshkoff
obtained an emigrants passport through the Bureau of Ru--
ssian Emigrants at Harbin. Horoshkoff stated that he did
not apply for an emigrants passport previously as he was w
waiting for an U.S.A. visa. In May 1937 he arrived to
Shanghai from Harbin, as he stated for a short period
but was forces to remain here permanently owing to cir-
cumstances. According to his statement he had intention
to leave Shanghai for Africa or South America as a sailor
on board of some ship, but could not realise his wish.
Arrived at Shanghai Horoshkoff was in hard financial
circumstances and worked casually as a book keeper.
Few years ago he made aquaintance and became sweetheart of
Mrs. Lidia Borstling, German citizen of Russian origin,
nee Merkuloff, born on 23-3-1900 at Nikolaevsk, Siberia,
wife of Richard Borstling,German merchant residing at Pass
-age 186, House 9, Av, Albert, Kelmscot Garden. It is
said that Mrs. L. Borstling supported Horoshkoff and fi-
nanced him when Nehoroshkoff established "Little Book
Store" at No. 102l Av. Joffre. Horoshkoff is dealing with
old books and different second hands articles. He
rents the premises of his store from one Sinani, Russian
Jew, for $100 dollars per months. Horoshkoff continues to
work casually as a book keeper. According to his statemer
statement to the R.E.C. his income is $800 per month but
probably it is not correct as the business is going
apparently well and he as he employed as a shop assistant
certain Ludmila Emelianovna Vasilenko, Russian emigrant
born on 3-12-1923 at Maritime Province residing at No.
516 Av. Albert.

报告
- 2 -

警署........................................ 档案号.................... 日期....................................

主题：
据其陈述，直至1937年，Horoshkoff 持有一本过期的苏联护照。1937年，Horoshkoff 通过哈尔滨的俄罗斯流亡者局获得了一本流亡者护照。Horoshkoff 称，此前未申请流亡者护照是因为他在等待美国签证。1937年5月，他从哈尔滨抵达上海，据称原计划只作短期停留，但因 circumstances（形势/情况）所迫而不得不永久留在此地。据其陈述，他曾打算作为某艘船上的水手离开上海前往非洲或南美洲，但未能实现这一愿望。
抵达上海后，Horoshkoff 经济状况困难，临时从事簿记工作。
几年前，他结识了 Lidia Borstling 女士并成为其情人。Lidia Borstling 女士是德籍公民，俄裔，婚前姓 Merkuloff，1900年3月23日出生于西伯利亚尼古拉耶夫斯克，是居住在阿尔伯特路（Av. Albert）凯尔姆斯科特花园（Kelmscot Garden）186弄9号的德国商人 Richard Borstling 的妻子。据说，当 Horoshkoff 在霞飞路（Av. Joffre）1021号开设“小书店”（Little Book Store）时，L. Borstling 女士曾资助他并提供资金。Horoshkoff 经营旧书和各种二手物品。他向一位名叫 Sinani 的俄罗斯犹太人租用店面，月租金为100美元。Horoshkoff 继续临时从事簿记工作。根据他向俄罗斯流亡者委员会（R.E.C.）的陈述，他的月收入为800美元，但这可能不实，因为生意显然不错，而且他雇佣了一名店员 Ludmila Emelianovna Vasilenko，她是俄罗斯流亡者，1923年12月3日出生于滨海省，居住在阿尔伯特路516号。

page_data.en:
F.M. 3
G. 500-1-43

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT
- 3 -

Station........................................ File No.................... Date....................................

SUBJECT:
About six months ago Horoshkoff broke his relations
with Mrs. L. Borstling who previously often visited his
shop where he resides since April 1942. It is said that
L. Borstling quarrelled with Horoshkoff and on one occa-
sion made trouble in his store throwing books on the
floor.
It should be pointed out that Horoshkoff has a
success among the women, who are the main customers
of his store.
Horoshkoff has a reputation of a reserved, rather
rude mannered person, who has few male friends. No-
thing could be ascertained regarding his alleged poli-
tical activity mentioned in attached anonymous letter.
Horoshkoff seems not much interested in political questi
ons and during the conversation mentioned that he would
with pleasure leave Shanghai. It is quite possible
that Horoshkoff above-mentioned allegations regarding
subversive political work of Horoshkoff was written
by Mrs. L. Borstling or other woman his former sweet-
heart with whom Horoshkoff broke relations, or by
jealouse husband or sweetheart of one of them. Horo-
shkoff married on May 1934 at Vladivostok a Russian
girl name unknown who left to U.S.A. from Harbin in
1936 (?) In Horoshkoff Pao Cha form is mentioned
that he is still married and in his Application to
Russian Emigrants Committee he stated that he is divor-
ced. Horoshkoff stated that he has father Feder Nico-
laevich Horoshkoff, brothers Sergey, Vladimir and two
sisters Maria and Zinaida residing in USSR but their
address is unknown to him.

（印：刑特
第五科
18.3.17
下）

报告
- 3 -

警署........................................ 档案号.................... 日期....................................

主题：
大约六个月前，Horoshkoff 与 L. Borstling 女士断绝了关系，后者此前经常光顾他的店铺，而他自1942年4月起便居住在该店内。据说 L. Borstling 与 Horoshkoff 发生争吵，有一次还在他的店里闹事，将书扔在地上。
值得注意的是，Horoshkoff 在女性顾客中很受欢迎，这些女性是他书店的主要客源。
Horoshkoff 的名声是一个矜持、举止相当粗鲁的人，男性朋友很少。关于附呈匿名信中提到的所谓政治活动，未能查明任何情况。Horoshkoff 似乎对政治问题不太感兴趣，并在谈话中提到他很乐意离开上海。上述关于 Horoshkoff 从事颠覆性政治工作的指控，很有可能是由 L. Borstling 女士或其他与他断绝关系的前情妇，或是她们当中某人的嫉妒丈夫或情人所写。Horoshkoff 于1934年5月在符拉迪沃斯托克娶了一位名字不详的俄罗斯姑娘，该女子于1936年（？）从哈尔滨前往美国。在 Horoshkoff 的保甲登记表（Pao Cha form）中提到他已婚，而在向俄罗斯流亡者委员会提交的申请书中，他声称自己已离婚。Horoshkoff 称，他有父亲 Feder Nicolaevich Horoshkoff，兄弟 Sergey、Vladimir 以及两个姐妹 Maria 和 Zinaida 居住在苏联，但他不知道他们的地址。

（印：刑特
第五科

下发）

Personal.
Supt. Kobayashi （印：…）

Sir,
With reference to previous reports re a certain Mr. Horoshkoff,
a Soviet citizen, whose activities have been checked for the last
two months: it is in the opinion of the writer of this report that the
above individual is definitely engaged in subversive and political
work.
It has been established as a fact that several persons have been
approached by the said person in question, with a view to procure a □□
spacious room, and offering a considerable sum, for which, as it
does appear, the said sum does not suitably apply to his means as a
dealer of second hand books. The person in question, as may appropria-
tely be deducted has some financial connection with the Bank of
Moscow (the Soviet Bank) and the latter, it is suggested, holds
special funds for distribution among political workers.
It is presumed, that with the best of returns from the said
book store (located on Avenue Joffre), the total asset may come to
about $500 or $600 per mensem, taking into consideration his de-
ductions from the above sum as for living expenses, rent and others,
there seems no possibility for this sort of propriety to cover half
the expenses which one may envolve in political work except for this
purpose.
Another fact shews the activities to be of political trend, is □□
his distribution of old and new Soviet journals, free or with a
minimum charge to persons,, members of the Soviet Club and young
females working in Beauty shops and other persons seemingly of poor □□
class.
When Mr. Horoshkoff was casually approached on the subject of
renting a room, and asked if the rent of $500 would be acceptable to
him, the answer came that he was not interested in the amount, but
in the space which it would provide, giving it a reason that he has □□
quite a few friends who visit him often and therefore the space
would be considered rather than the sum.
It is presumed, and this presumption is well founded, that his
"friends" are of political nature and himself a head of a nest with
fixed instructions as to his activities in this city.
It is also suggested, that political propaganda does not
exclude the Chinese population, as regards war news and other anti-
Nippon Great East Asia War.
It could not have been possible, for the time being, to establish
the identities of persons with whom he comes into contact, but it
has been ascertained that among his so called friends, there has been
a few women involved.
A further report will be submitted with regard the above
mentioned person and details will follow re the other persons working
under him.

Yours Obediently.
page_data.zh:
私人信件。
Kobayashi 警司 （印：…）

先生，
关于此前有关某位 Horoshkoff 先生（苏联公民）的报告，其活动在过去两个月中受到监视：本报告撰写者认为，上述个人确实从事颠覆性和政治工作。
经查证属实，该人曾接触数人，意图租赁一间宽敞的房间，并愿意支付巨额租金。鉴于其作为二手书商的收入水平，这笔款项显然与其财力不符。据此推断，该人与莫斯科银行（苏联银行）存在某种财务联系，而该行据称设有专门用于分配给政治工作人员的基金。
据推测，即使该书店（位于霞飞路）收益极佳，其总资产每月约为500或600美元，考虑到从中扣除生活费、房租及其他开支，这笔财产似乎不可能覆盖政治工作所需费用的一半，除非另有目的。
另一项显示其活动具有政治倾向的事实是，他向苏联俱乐部成员、在美容院工作的年轻女性以及其他看似贫困阶层的人士免费或以最低收费分发新旧苏联期刊。
当有人随意向 Horoshkoff 先生提及租房事宜，并询问500美元的租金是否可接受时，他回答说他对金额不感兴趣，而是看重空间大小，理由是他有不少朋友经常来访，因此更考虑空间而非金额。
据推测，且这一推测有充分依据，他的“朋友”具有政治性质，而他本人则是一个巢穴的头目，接收关于在本市活动的固定指令。
此外还指出，政治宣传并不排除中国民众，内容涉及战争新闻及其他反日大东亚战争的宣传。
目前尚无法确定与他接触的人员身份，但已查明在其所谓的朋友中，涉及几名女性。
将就上述人员提交进一步报告，并将随后提供在其手下工作的其他人员的详细情况。

此致
敬礼。

据霍罗什科夫（Horoshkoff）称，直至1937年，他持有一本已过期的苏联护照。1937年，霍罗什科夫通过哈尔滨的俄罗斯难民局获得了一本难民护照。霍罗什科夫称，他此前未申请难民护照是因为一直在等待美国签证。据其所述，他于1937年5月从哈尔滨抵达上海，原计划只作短期停留，但因 circumstances（原文如此，意指“情况”或“局势”）所迫而不得不永久留居此地。据其称，他曾打算以船员身份乘船离开上海前往非洲或南美洲，但未能实现这一愿望。

霍罗什科夫抵沪时经济状况困难，临时从事簿记员工作。数年前，他结识了莉迪亚·博斯特林夫人（Mrs. Lidia Borstling），并与之成为恋人。博斯特林夫人为德籍公民，俄裔，婚前姓克尔库洛夫（Kerkuloff），1900年3月23日生于西伯利亚尼古拉耶夫斯克（Nikolaevsk），系德国商人理查德·博斯特林（Richard Borstling）之妻，居住于阿尔伯特路（Av. Albert）凯尔姆斯科特花园（Kelmscot Garden）9号186弄。据称，当霍罗什科夫在霞飞路（Av. Joffre）1021号开设“小书店”（Little Book Store）时，博斯特林夫人曾资助并为其提供资金。霍罗什科夫经营旧书及各种二手物品。他向一名俄籍犹太人辛纳尼（Sinani）租用店面，月租金为100美元。霍罗什科夫继续临时从事簿记员工作。据其向俄罗斯难民委员会（R.E.C.）申报，其月收入为800美元，但此数据可能不实，因为其生意显然经营良好，且他雇佣了一名店员柳德米拉·埃梅利亚诺夫娜·瓦西连科（Ludmila Emelianovna Vasilenko），该员为俄籍难民，1923年12月3日生于滨海省（Maritime Province），现居住于阿尔伯特路516号。

page_data.en:
- 3 -

About six months ago Horoshkoff broke his relations
with Mrs. L. Borstling who previously often visited his
shop where he resides since April 1942. It is said that
L. Borstling quarrelled with Horoshkoff and on one occa-
sion made trouble in his store throwing books on the
floor.
It should be pointed out that Horoshkoff has a
success among the women, who are the main customers
of his store.
Horoshkoff has a reputation of a reserved, rather
rude mannered person, who has few male friends. No-
thing could be ascertained regarding his alleged poli-
tical activity mentioned in attached anonymous letter.
Horoshkoff seems not much interested in political quest-
ions and during the conversation mentioned that he would
with pleasure leave Shanghai. It is quite possible
that Horoshkoff above-mentioned allegations regarding
subversive political work of Horoshkoff was written
by Mrs. L. Borstling or other woman his former sweet-
heart with whom Horoshkoff broke relations, or by
jealous husband or sweetheart of one of them. Horo-
shkoff married on May 1934 at Vladivostok a Russian
girl name unknown who left to U.S.A. from Harbin in
1936 (?) In Horoshkoff Pao Cha form is mentioned
that he is still married and in his Application to
Russian Emigrants Committee he stated that he is divor-
ced. Horoshkoff stated that he has father Fedor Nico-
laevich Horoshkoff, brothers: Sergey, Vladimir and two
sisters Maria and Zinaida residing in USSR but their
address is unknown to him.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

约六个月前，霍罗什科夫与博斯特林夫人断绝了关系。此前，博斯特林夫人常光顾他的店铺，自1942年4月起，霍罗什科夫便居住在该店内。据称，博斯特林夫人与霍罗什科夫发生争吵，并曾在其店内闹事，将书籍扔在地上。

值得注意的是，霍罗什科夫在女性顾客中颇受欢迎，而这些女性正是其店铺的主要客源。

霍罗什科夫给人的印象是性格孤僻、举止相当粗鲁，男性朋友很少。关于附件匿名信中提及的所谓政治活动，未能查明任何事实。霍罗什科夫似乎对政治问题兴趣不大，并在谈话中表示他很乐意离开上海。上述有关霍罗什科夫从事颠覆性政治工作的指控，很有可能是由博斯特林夫人、或与霍罗什科夫断绝关系的另一位前女友、或是她们当中某人的嫉妒丈夫或情人所撰写。霍罗什科夫于1934年5月在符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostok）娶了一名俄罗斯女子，姓名不详，该女子于1936年（？）从哈尔滨前往美国。在霍罗什科夫的保甲登记表（Pao Cha form）中提到他仍处于已婚状态，而在其向俄罗斯难民委员会提交的申请中，他则声称自己已离婚。霍罗什科夫称，其父为费奥多尔·尼古拉耶维奇·霍罗什科夫（Fedor Nicolaevich Horoshkoff），兄弟有谢尔盖（Sergey）、弗拉基米尔（Vladimir），姐妹有玛丽亚（Maria）和齐奈达（Zinaida），均居住在苏联，但他不知晓他们的地址。

- 4 -

In Horoshkoff's application to the Russian Emigrants
Committee are mentioned as guarantors Nicolay Boriso-
vich Chukreeff and Ludmila Emelianovna Vasilonko both
residing, at No. 516 Av. Albert.

Any further information of interest regarding G.F.
Horoshkoff will be duly submitted.

....................
                  D.S.

Officer i/c
Foreign Affairs
Crime & Special Branch

- 4 -

在霍罗什科夫向俄罗斯难民委员会提交的申请中，列明的担保人为尼古拉·鲍里索维奇·丘克雷夫（Nicolay Borisovich Chukreeff）和柳德米拉·埃梅利亚诺夫娜·瓦西连科（Ludmila Emelianovna Vasilonko），两人均居住于阿尔伯特路516号。

有关G.F.霍罗什科夫的任何其他感兴趣的情报，将及时呈报。

....................
                  D.S.

外事组
